subject: Ephemeral audit access exception — gating questions & rollout path
messages:
From: Linda Park <linda@acmehealth.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: short-term audit access exception for clinical pilot

Hi Tessa,

We're ramping a two-week pilot of Acme's clinical ingestion flow with Redwood next month and hit a gating requirement from our security team — they want a short-lived audit-access path so their SOC lead can review raw request/response traces during the pilot window.

Specifically they asked: can Redwood provide ephemeral access to audit logs (read-only) scoped to the pilot tenant for a 14-day window, after which logs should be auto-archived to our S3 and access revoked? They also want confirmation that BYOK keys are not exposed to Redwood personnel and a simple checklist we can hand to procurement.

I've attached an evidence matrix and a short request doc. Can you confirm whether this is feasible and what the approval flow looks like? Procurement is waiting on an answer to finish the PO.

Thanks,
Linda Park
Security Program Manager, Acme Health

Attachments: acme_evidence_matrix.csv, ephemeral-access-request.docx

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Linda Park <linda@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: short-term audit access exception for clinical pilot

Marissa / Karthik — quick triage request from Acme (see attached). Linda's asking for an ephemeral-read-only audit access path limited to the pilot tenant for 14 days, plus proof that BYOK key materials won't be exposed. Procurement wants the answer this week.

Key constraints I see:
- We can provide scoped audit exports and a temporary secure link, but need to confirm retention/auto-archive behavior and exact RBAC semantics.
- BYOK: we support customer-managed keys for storage; we must confirm whether any operational debugging would require key escrow access (should be no).
- Evidence required: sample audit schema, export process, and a one-page steps checklist for procurement + a signed attestation from Security if needed.

Can you two propose an ops pattern we can offer that minimizes engineering changes? Prefer a config-only flow (tenant flag + timebound presigned access) rather than a bespoke exception. If we do a short-lived admin grant, what's the approval path (security sign-off + legal digest)?

Linda — we'll circle back with a recommended path and a checklist by EOD Thursday PST.

—Tessa
Product Security, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Linda Park <linda@acmehealth.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 10:26:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: short-term audit access exception for clinical pilot

Thanks for flagging — quick proposal below (ops + minimal infra impact):

Proposal (pilot-mode ephemeral audit access):
- Implementation: tenant-scoped export job that writes audit bundles to the customer's S3 (customer BYOK enforced). The job emits a single time-bound presigned URL for a single ZIP containing the requested traces. Access token expires in 14 days. No change to runtime; uses existing export pipeline.
- Access model: read-only presigned URL delivered to the named Acme security lead. Redwood engineers will not hold the presigned URL beyond delivery. We will not decrypt or access BYOK-encrypted artifacts.
- Audit controls: each export is accompanied by a signed manifest (SHA256) and an export event logged in our internal audit ledger with immutable timestamp.
- Approval path: Product Security (Tessa) + Ops-on-call sign-off to run the export job; legal to approve the attestation wording. No infra change needed if Acme accepts S3 destination + presigned URL flow.

Open questions for Acme:
1) Which S3 bucket (customer-managed) should we write to and can we get a short S3 ACL for the export job?
2) Confirm the exact time window (14 days OK?).
3) Do you need us to include request/response payloads or just metadata + timestamps?

If this looks acceptable I'll draft the procurement checklist and a one-paragraph attestation for Legal. Karthik — if you can confirm the export job has the necessary RBAC and that presigned URLs can be revoked post-window, we can send to Acme today.

—Marissa
Director, Compliance Integrations

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Linda Park <linda@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Dec 2026 16:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: short-term audit access exception for clinical pilot

All — confirmed from infra:
- Export job exists and can target a customer-managed S3 with customer BYOK. We generate a single presigned URL that becomes invalid after the configured TTL. There is also an internal revoke flow (token blacklist) we can run if emergency revoke is needed.
- We do not store customer KMS keys and have no operational access to key material; encryption/decryption occurs only in the customer's environment when they download the bundle.

Next steps (action items):
1) Linda — provide S3 bucket name, principal for delivery, and final scope (payloads vs metadata) by EOD Friday.
2) Marissa — draft the procurement checklist + attestation text and loop in Legal (I'll include a short tech appendix stating we support revocation + signed manifests).
3) Tessa — approve Product Security sign-off once checklist + attestation are ready.

I'll stand by for details and can run a test export to a sandbox bucket if helpful.

-Karthik
Sr. Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
